title: Request for an Electrically Dimmable Cabin Window Retrofit on the Delivered Fleet

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Cabin Window Assembly

abstract: Operator request to retrofit electrically dimmable cabin windows across a sub-fleet for cabin product reasons, closed by engineering with an alternative offered because the window frame and the electrical provision on the delivered aircraft cannot carry the installation.

sections.request: We are refreshing the cabin product on twenty-two aircraft next year and our commercial department would like the shades replaced by the electrically dimmable windows that are becoming standard elsewhere. The pull-down shades are the single most commented-on item in our cabin survey, mostly because they stick and because passengers argue about them on daylight sectors. We understand this is a significant change and we are prepared to fund it, but we need to know now whether it is possible, because the rest of the cabin refresh programme is being ordered in the autumn and we cannot come back to the windows afterwards without opening the cabin twice.
sections.background: We asked the same question of the airframer of our other fleet three years ago and it was done there, so we know the technology works in service. We have twenty-two aircraft in the affected range, all CIRRANE-13, all with the same cabin layout. Our engineering department has looked at the window surround and thinks the space is there, but has no view on the electrical side. We have not costed it ourselves beyond a rough allowance.
sections.expected_outcome: A yes or no before the end of the third quarter, with an indicative price and downtime if it is a yes. If it is a no we would like to understand whether it becomes possible on a later build standard, so that we can plan the fleet renewal around it rather than around the cabin refresh.

type_data.business_justification: Cabin survey scores place the pull-down shade at the top of the passenger complaint list on daylight sectors, and the operator is committing to a cabin refresh that would have to be re-opened later if the window is not addressed at the same time.
type_data.closure_note: Closed without a modification. The delivered window frame on aircraft in the requested range carries no electrical provision at the reveal and the surround structure would have to be re-qualified for a powered pane, which is a major change on a pressure boundary rather than a cabin refresh item. A separate change is already in pre-analysis to bring the window frame drainage and the reveal interface to a common standard, and the electrical provision can only sensibly be considered on top of that. Engineering offered the operator the improved shade cassette and a revised lubrication task as an interim measure, and undertook to revisit the request once the frame standard is fixed.
